newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman streamline taxes on foreign, local firms.
newsitem.headline: Oman streamline taxes on foreign, local firms.

text.p: Oman, seeking to lure foreign capital needed to diversify its oil-based economy, on Tuesday began unveiling new amendments to company tax laws.

According to details from the finance ministry on new laws decreed by Sultan Qaboos bin Said last month, all firms listed on the Muscat Securities Market which have foreign shareholders stand to benefit the most.

Although Oman has the most open economy in the region, with rules on foreign ownership more liberal than in other Gulf states, the previous tax system discriminated against companies with foreign shareholders.

The amendments kept unchanged the 5.0 to 7.5 percent tax paid by fully Omani-owned firms. But they cut taxes on public shareholding companies with foreign partners to 5.0-7.5 percent from between 15 to 30 percent before.
This applies to listed firms in which Omanis own at least 51 percent of shares and 40 percent of its capital is offered in a public subscription.

"This will encourage investors to invest their funds in public shareholding companies...And will encourage other existing companies to transform into public shareholding companies, which will reflect positively on the economic situation in Oman," said a copy of the new rules.

The changes streamlined five-year tax exemptions on all companies working in industries, mining, fishing and fish canning, tourism and agriculture. Before that, only fully Omani-owned companies benefitted from such exemptions, which will be renewable for another five years.
The new laws take effect once they are published in the official gazette later this month.
